loading_notes: Catalogue: e2er-data gutenberg books --languages en --topic fiction --author-year-start S --author-year-end E --limit 320 --table gutenberg_books_cK (S,E as in each table's series). The frame is only the 320 most popular catalogue rows per cohort search (popularity-sorted). The catalogue filter selects authors ALIVE in the span, so it is only a candidate frame; the cohort is assigned from author_birth_year in build_data.py. Several searches per cohort (topics novel, fiction, romance, adventure) may be concatenated in the build script, never in the loaded tables.

Texts: e2er-data gutenberg text --ids <20 ids> --table gutenberg_texts_cK. The 20 ids per cohort are drawn by build_data.py logic with a fixed seed (20261014) from the eligible frame, and written to data/sample_ids.csv before loading so the load is reproducible. Loads are at most 20 books each.

Word counts are known only after the texts are loaded, so the 30,000-token rule is applied after loading and may shrink a cohort below 20; then every cohort is cut to the smallest n (equal n per cohort) and the shortfall is reported in data_summary.md.

fields.doc_id: 'pg' + Gutenberg ebook number; unique key of the corpus table
fields.title: catalogue title
fields.author: first author as in the catalogue (one author only)
fields.author_birth_year: integer, as the Gutenberg/Gutendex catalogue records it; the only basis of the cohort and the only time axis (no publication year is looked up or used)
fields.cohort: c1 1770-1799, c2 1800-1819, c3 1820-1839, c4 1840-1859, c5 1860-1879, c6 1880-1899; exactly one per novel by birth year (c1 is 30 years wide, the others 20; this is stated in the paper)
fields.word_count: number of tokens under the recorded token_pattern (before stop-word removal)
fields.file_sha256: SHA-256 of the text as analysed (UTF-8), recorded in corpus_manifest.json
fields.text: book text with Gutenberg header/footer removed by the connector, and front/back matter cut by build_data.py

inclusion_rules: subjects or bookshelves contain Fiction/Novel/Romance/Adventure/Detective/Historical-type terms, and do not contain Poetry, Drama, Short stories, Essays, Letters, Children's, Juvenile, Biography; books with a translator in the catalogue record are excluded (translations)
exactly one author, with author_birth_year in 1770-1899
has_plain_text is true and copyright is not true
word_count >= 30,000 tokens (novel length; excludes novellas and stories), applied after the texts are loaded because counts are unknown before

de-duplication: one edition per work, keyed on normalised title + author; keep the lowest ebook number whose text is complete; also drop texts with identical SHA-256; omnibus volumes and multi-volume sets that contain several titles are dropped

boilerplate: connector removes the Gutenberg header, footer and licence; build_data.py additionally removes contents lists, prefaces/introductions by editors, transcriber's notes and illustration lists where detectable; what was cut is recorded per document
sample_balance: Stratified random sample, equal n (target 20) per cohort, drawn with seed 20261014 after filtering. At most 2 novels per author per cohort (cap prevents one author dominating). Gender, genre and nationality are not balanced because the catalogue does not hold them reliably; the paper reports the author-count and the share of the corpus from the largest author per cohort, and runs the main comparison with each document weighted equally (mean of per-document rates) alongside pooled rates per 10,000 tokens. Length varies across cohorts; results are per 10,000 tokens and the median length per cohort is reported.

weather_dictionary.note: Frozen in corpus_design.json. Exact word forms only, no wildcards at all; inflections and plurals are listed explicitly, no lemma table. 'hail' (greeting, 'within hail') and 'storming' (storming a fort) are excluded. Ambiguous terms kept and covered by the hand-checked validation sample: shower/showers, thunder forms, icy, cloud forms, plus wind (verb), sun (Sunday, surname), figurative storm/cloud, and the surnames Snow/Rain/Frost; precision is reported per category.

unavailable: Publication year is not used at all (not looked up, no robustness check); the time axis is the author's birth year as the catalogue records it. Author gender, nationality and genre are not in the catalogue and are not analysed.
Other corpora (Standard Ebooks, ELTeC, Chadwyck-Healey) are not among the available sources, so the sampling frame is Project Gutenberg only.
